checks.citation: 38 U.S.C. 1703D(a)(1), (a)(4), (d)(1), (g)(1)(A), (i)(2)-(3) (uscode.house.gov text current through Pub. L. 119-142, Nov. 10, 2026; last amended 2018); VA fact sheet IB-10-1379 (updated Jan. 24, 2022)
checks.quote: the Secretary shall pay for hospital care, medical services, or extended care services furnished by health care entities or providers under this chapter within 45 calendar days upon receipt of a clean paper claim or 30 calendar days upon receipt of a clean electronic claim.
checks.correction: Correct as stated. Two additions. (1) The overdue test in (d)(1) reads: 'Any claim that has not been denied with notice, made pending with notice, or paid to the health care entity or provider by the Secretary shall be overdue if the notice or payment is not received by the entity provider within the time periods specified in subsection (a).' A pend notice also stops the clock, so a letter must say that no payment, no denial notice and no pend notice was received. (2) For a medical practice, a better VA cite than the dental sheet is fact sheet IB-10-1186 'Community Care Network (CCN)' (updated Jan. 27, 2022), Q8: 'Community providers under CCN will be paid within 30 days of submitting a clean claim to their region's respective third-party administrator. checks.quote: If a claim is denied, the Secretary shall, within 45 calendar days of denial for a paper claim and 30 calendar days of denial for an electronic claim, notify the health care entity or provider of the reason for denying the claim and what, if any, additional information is required to process the claim.
checks.correction: Correct. (a)(3) verified: 'Upon the receipt of the additional information, the Secretary shall ensure that the claim is paid, denied, or otherwise adjudicated within 30 calendar days from the receipt of the requested information.' checks.citation: 38 U.S.C. 1703D(d)(2)(A)-(B); 31 U.S.C. 3902(a)-(b); Treasury Prompt Payment interest rate table (page last updated Sept. 29, 2026); 84 FR 26301 (June 5, 2019, VCCP final rule, FR Doc. 2019-11575)
checks.quote: If a claim is overdue under this subsection, the Secretary may, under the requirements established by subsection (a) and consistent with the provisions of chapter 39 of title 31 (commonly referred to as the “Prompt Payment Act”), require that interest be paid on clean claims.
checks.correction: Correct. Rates verified on the Treasury table: Jul-Dec 2026 4.75% (Vol. 91, No. 130, July 9, 2026, p. 42594); Jan-Jun 2026 4.125% (Vol. 91, No. 22, Feb. 3, 2026, p. 5035); Jan-Jun and Jul-Dec 2025 4.625%. The 2019 promise is at 84 FR 26301: 'VA will be undertaking future rulemaking to implement the prompt pay provisions of section 1703D, which will include provisions ... addressing interest on overdue claims'. A Federal Register API search of VA documents since 2019 for '1703D', 'prompt payment', 'overdue claims' and 'clean claim(s)' found no final rule. For exact figures in letters (the False Claims Act constraint in VA-22): 31 U.S.C. 3902(a) uses the rate 'in effect at the time the agency accrues the obligation to pay a late payment interest penalty', and 5 CFR 1315.10(a)(1) and (a)(9) compute it 'from the day after the payment due date through the payment date at the interest rate in effect on the day after the payment due date' on 'a 360 day year'; interest under $1.00 is not required (1315.10(c)(5)).

L. 115-251 sec. 204) from 'shall deduct' to 'may deduct' and adds 'may use any other means authorized by another provision of law to correct or recover overpayments'. Before any letter asserts a TRICARE interest duty, a person must open https://manuals.health.mil/pages/DisplayManualHtmlFile/2024-08-07/AsOf/tot5/c3s2.html in a browser and confirm the current change and its wording; until then, letters may only request interest under 1095c(a)(2).

missing: 32 CFR 199.7(h)(4) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-08-17/title-32.xml?part=199): 'Benefit under $1. If the CHAMPUS benefit is determined to be under $1, payment is waived.' TRICARE pays nothing on a benefit under $1, so a TRICARE line worth less than $1 cannot be recovered by any letter. The owner's 'even $0.60' rule must exclude TRICARE benefit amounts under $1.

32 CFR 199.8(d)(1)(vii) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-08-17/title-32.xml?part=199): 'In the case of a beneficiary enrolled in a MA-PD plan who receives items or services for which payment may be made under both the MA-PD plan and CHAMPUS/TRICARE, a claim for the beneficiary's normal out-of-pocket costs under the MA-PD plan may be submitted for CHAMPUS/TRICARE payment.' A TRICARE-eligible patient in Humana or another Medicare Advantage plan can have the MA copay or coinsurance billed to TRICARE For Life (within 1 year, 199.7(d)). The cap is in (d)(1)(ii) and the same paragraph. (d)(1)(viii): 'CHAMPUS is second payer to other third-party payers of health insurance, including Medicare supplemental plans', so with a Medigap plan TRICARE pays after the Medigap plan. This is a 'secondary never billed' source the researcher did not list.

32 CFR 199.11(f)(6)(ii)(B)-(E), (f)(6)(v), (f)(4), (d) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-08-17/title-32.xml?part=199): TRICARE recoupments. The demand letter must give 'The right to inspect and copy TRICARE records pertaining to the debt' and 'The opportunity to request an administrative review by the TRICARE contractor; and that such a request must be received by the TRICARE contractor within 90 days from the date of the initial demand letter'; payment is due in 30 days; interest at the Treasury Current Value of Funds rate runs from the demand letter and is waived if paid within 30 days. 'No collection by offset may be undertaken unless the debtor has been sent a written demand for payment, including the procedural safeguards described in paragraph (f)(6)(ii)' (narrow exception). (f)(4): for denials caused by 'a change, clarification or interpretation', 'no recoupment action need be taken to recover funds expended prior to the effective date'. (d): a pending appeal 'may provide a basis for the suspension of collection'. The researcher covered VA and Optum recoupments but not TRICARE's.

32 CFR 199.17(a)(7)(ii) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-08-17/title-32.xml?part=199): 'any State or local law relating to health insurance, prepaid health plans, or other health care delivery or financing methods is preempted and does not apply in connection with TRICARE regional contracts.' This is the exact citation for the researcher's 'does not apply' point: Kentucky and Indiana prompt-pay laws cannot be used against Humana Military on TRICARE claims. No comparable VA preemption rule for CCN was found in 38 CFR part 17.

32 CFR 199.10(b)(4)(i)-(v), (a)(1)(i)(F), (a)(9) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-08-17/title-32.xml?part=199): a TRICARE reconsideration notice 'must contain' the issues, 'The provisions of law, regulation, policies, and guidelines that apply to the issue or issues under appeal', a discussion of the information, the rationale, and appeal rights when the amount in dispute is $50 or more; every adverse initial notice 'shall include a statement of the beneficiary's or provider's right to appeal'. This counters a boilerplate (or AI-written) denial: the practice can demand the missing elements. Risk: (a)(9) lets an appeal decision 'address all pertinent issues ... (for example, the entire episode of care in the appeal)', so an appeal can reopen paid lines.

A, title VII, sec. 731(a)-(b) (https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/t10/s1095c/): TRICARE claims processing on '(2) The documentation required to substantiate medical necessity for items and services that are covered under both the TRICARE program and the Medicare program' 'shall be identical to the claims processing requirements under the Medicare program'. This is stronger than 1095c(d) for records demands and medical-necessity denials.

Optum VA CCN Provider Manual (version 2026 1102), p. 47 and p. 43 (https://vacommunitycare.com/api/vaccnportal/v1/webcomponentcode/trainingdoc/ccnProvManual/ccnPrManual): 'Claims for ancillary services will be processed in accordance with CMS NCCI, MUE and related edits' and 'All providers are required to follow CMS billing and coding requirements outlined in the Medicare Claims Processing Manual, unless their VA CCN agreement states otherwise.' The CCN underpayment and edit checks can reuse Medicare logic.

Humana Military TRICARE Provider Handbook, East Region 2026, p. 18 (https://www.humanamilitary.com/content/dam/sites/humana-military-com/provider/tricare-provider-handbook.pdf): 'A network provider who submits a claim for an unauthorized service is subject to a penalty of up to 50 percent the TRICARE-allowable charge and the beneficiary may be held harmless.' This cuts against the practice for referral and authorization misses (network providers only).

VA Community Care 'Provider claims' page (updated Oct. 20, 2026) (https://department.va.gov/vha/community-care/provider-claims/): 'Supporting documentation for claims processing applies only to unauthorized emergency care claims. It is not required for authorized care claims.' This applies to claims VA processes itself (VCA, VA-paid). For CCN claims, Optum's separate records duty above still applies.

84 FR 26301 (June 5, 2019) (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2019-06-05/html/2019-11575.htm): 'We clarify that the compensation options are part of the contract between VA and the TPA.' VA's own statement that CCN payment terms live in the VA-Optum contract and the provider's Optum agreement, which supports the researcher's open question about the practice's VA CCN payment appendix and dispute clause.
